title: Percent Problems
subtitle: Tax, Tips, Discounts & Percent Change
bounds: PROTOCOL §4b percents. Percents: tip 10, 20, 25; tax 10, 20; discount 10, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50, 75; markup 10, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50; simple interest 10, 20, 25 a year for 2-5 years; percent change 10, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50, 75; percent error 10, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50; a second step 10, 20 (tax) or 10, 20, 25 (off). Every percent is taken of a whole it divides cleanly, so the hidden ÷ is a times-table fact: tens of percent of 20-90 in tens (10% first, then × 1-9), 25% and 75% of 8-40 in fours, 50% also of evens 4-20. Each amount added or subtracted (tip, tax, discount, markup, interest, change, miss) is a whole number 2-20; every whole, new price and total is 100 or less. A percent change or error is the change over the original (actual) value, itself one of those clean wholes. Interest: yearly amount 2-10, years 2-5, interest 20 or less. Two steps: the second percent is of a new whole that is again a clean one. Answers are whole dollars or whole percents. Wrong choices: whatever the misreading gives, up to 999 (a decimal percent like 0.25% is the 'forgot to scale' slip).

tiers.name: Tax & Tip
tiers.description: Find the tip or tax, then add it on to get the total.

tiers.name: Discounts
tiers.description: Find the discount, then take it off to get the sale price.

tiers.name: Markup & Interest
tiers.description: Markups add to a price. Simple interest repeats every year.

tiers.name: Percent Change
tiers.description: Find the percent increase or decrease from the original value.

tiers.name: Error & Two Steps
tiers.description: Percent error, and two percents one after the other.

PART_ONLY.student: That is only the extra amount. Add it to the price to get the total.
PART_ONLY.teacher: Stops after finding the tip, tax or markup and reports it as the total.

DISCOUNT_ONLY.student: That is only the discount. Take it off the price to see what you pay.
DISCOUNT_ONLY.teacher: Stops after finding the discount and reports it as the sale price.

PERCENT_AS_DOLLARS.student: The % number is not dollars. Find that percent OF the price first.
PERCENT_AS_DOLLARS.teacher: Uses the percent number itself as the dollar amount (20% of $40 treated as $20).

TENTH_FOR_ALL.student: Only 10% is 1/10 of the price. Find 10% first, then scale to the percent.
TENTH_FOR_ALL.teacher: Takes 10% of the whole whatever percent is asked (20% of $40 as $4).

SUBTRACTED.student: Tax, tips and markups add to the price. They do not take away.
SUBTRACTED.teacher: Subtracts a tip, tax or markup instead of adding it.

ADDED.student: A discount takes money off. Subtract it from the price.
ADDED.teacher: Adds the discount to the price instead of subtracting it.

TOTAL_FOR_PART.student: That is the total. The question asks only for the extra amount.
TOTAL_FOR_PART.teacher: Gives the price plus the tip, tax or markup when only the amount was asked.

SALE_FOR_SAVINGS.student: That is the sale price. The question asks how much you save.
SALE_FOR_SAVINGS.teacher: Gives the price after the discount when the discount itself was asked.

ONE_YEAR.student: That is one year. Simple interest repeats every year: times the years.
ONE_YEAR.teacher: Finds one year of simple interest and does not multiply by the years.

TOTAL_FOR_INTEREST.student: That is the balance. Interest is only what you earn on top.
TOTAL_FOR_INTEREST.teacher: Gives the starting amount plus interest when the interest alone was asked.

INTEREST_ONLY.student: That is only the interest. The balance is the start amount plus interest.
INTEREST_ONLY.teacher: Gives the interest earned when the total balance was asked.

DIFFERENCE_AS_PERCENT.student: A change of 5 is not 5%. Divide the change by the original (or actual) value.
DIFFERENCE_AS_PERCENT.teacher: Reports the size of the change (or miss) itself as the percent.

NEW_AS_BASE.student: Compare the change with the ORIGINAL amount, not the new one.
NEW_AS_BASE.teacher: Divides the change by the new value instead of the original.

RATIO_AS_CHANGE.student: That compares new to old. A percent change is only the part that changed.
RATIO_AS_CHANGE.teacher: Gives new/old as a percent (125%, 80%) instead of the change over the original.

DECIMAL_NOT_PERCENT.student: That is the decimal. Multiply by 100 to write it as a percent.
DECIMAL_NOT_PERCENT.teacher: Divides the change by the original but leaves it as a decimal, then writes %.

GUESS_AS_BASE.student: Percent error compares the miss with the ACTUAL value, not the guess.
GUESS_AS_BASE.teacher: Divides the miss by the guess instead of the actual value.

GUESS_RATIO.student: That is guess compared to actual. Percent error is only the miss.
GUESS_RATIO.teacher: Gives guess/actual as a percent (90%, 120%) instead of the miss over the actual.

FORGOT_SECOND.student: There is a second step. Take the second percent of the new price too.
FORGOT_SECOND.teacher: Stops after the first percent and ignores the second.

COMBINED_PERCENTS.student: Do one percent at a time. The second is of the new price, not the original.
COMBINED_PERCENTS.teacher: Combines the two percents (50% off, 10% tax as 40% off) or takes the second of the original.

SECOND_WRONG_WAY.student: Check the direction: tax and markups add, discounts take away.
SECOND_WRONG_WAY.teacher: Applies the second percent the wrong way (adds a discount, subtracts a tax).
